candidate.answerReason: Of the twelve equally likely ordered pairs, two are red-red and two are white-white, giving 4/12 = 1/3.

methods.label: Count ordered pairs by color
methods.explanation: Without replacement, there are \(4\times3=12\) outcomes in total. There are \(2\times1=2\) outcomes with 2 red balls and \(2\times1=2\) outcomes with 2 white balls, giving 4 favorable outcomes. The probability is \(4/12=1/3\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses elementary ordered pair counting, two disjoint color cases and fraction reduction.

methods.label: Count matches among the remaining balls
methods.explanation: Focus on the balls remaining after the first draw. If the first ball is red, the three remaining balls contain one red ball and two white balls, so exactly one of the three equally likely second draws matches. If the first ball is white, the remaining balls contain one white ball and two red balls, again giving exactly one matching draw out of three. These two cases cover every possible first color, and each gives the same probability. Therefore the probability of matching colors is \(\frac{1}{3}\).
methods.levelReason: The argument uses only the equally likely remaining balls and two exhaustive color cases, within Grade 9 probability.
